name: Carriage Sentry
description: A mobile Q machine follows its owner, then braces for half a second before firing. Shorter range and lost moving fire trade sustained output for relocation.

name: Pressure Charges
description: Q places an armed proximity charge instead of a turret. Up to two charges; one second arming, half-second visible fuse, ordinary control and finite explosions.

name: Anchor Circuit
description: Anchor every carriage, then recall it to follow. Commands share a short recovery and require fresh bracing.

name: Survey Drive
description: Order carriages to a fixed, legal point ahead of your aim. They travel there and hold formation.

name: Coil Lance
description: Earn a fourth active action: a carriage commits its aim, charges, then fires a piercing beam.

name: Prism Coils
description: Coil Lance becomes a three-lane sequence, sweeping a wider approach with separately timed rays.

name: Salvage Pulse
description: Earn a fifth active action: dismantle nearby carriages to recover part of Q deployment cooldown.

name: Rail Convergence
description: All surviving carriages commit converging rails, followed by a warned collapse at their shared mark.

name: Tripwire Couplers
description: Two ready plates share a visible clear tripwire. Crossing it commits both full fuses. Choose this or Safety Switch.

name: Safety Switch
description: Q during deployment cooldown or with both slots full holds or releases idle plates. A committed fuse cannot be interrupted. Choose this or Tripwire Couplers.

name: Firing Key
description: Add action 1: commit every ready owned plate to its full visible fuse, including held plates.

name: Breach Casings
description: Committed explosions also release a warned shaped jet along each plate's placed direction. Cover can shorten the warned lane.

name: Haul Line
description: Add action 2: winch a nearby idle plate to a legal aimed position, then fully rearm it. Its original lifetime remains.

name: Demolition Corridor
description: Remote-fire two clear linked plates, then release a warned demolition strip. Both plates must actually detonate; interrupted ground cancels the strip.

name: Field Screen
description: Q assembles a finite owned screen instead of a turret. It takes half a second to brace; friendly movement remains clear.

name: Longspan Panels
description: Build one broad screen with the same health spread over a longer frontage. Excludes Return Wings.

name: Return Wings
description: Build two angled side screens instead of a flat front. They share the original health budget and leave the central approach exposed. Excludes Longspan Panels.

name: Hinged Assembly
description: Add action1: fold and pivot a nearby owned screen group to a fixed aimed heading. Folded panels cannot block shots.

name: Field Maintenance
description: Add action2: stay still for a committed repair to one damaged owned wall. No player healing, shield or lifetime extension.

name: Linked Foundations
description: Maintain two separate Q screen groups at once. Each keeps its own original lifetime and assembly window.

name: Survey Frame
description: Evolve the hinge action to fold and shift a screen group toward a fixed work point before rebracing. Existing health and expiry remain.

name: Keystone Redoubt
description: Impossible Machine also assembles three finite cover panels on clear ground around its original position. The machine keeps its issued behavior; losing it removes its fortification.

name: Passing Shot
description: After Precision Burst, use action 1 within 1.2 seconds while holding movement: commit a 90-pixel, 0.3-second step and fire a separate 15-base-damage piercing round on arrival. No dodge immunity; blocked ground rejects without spending the opening.

name: Crossing Advance
description: Action 1 commits forward along your aim. Split its original follow-up damage between a departure round and an arrival round; aim again for the arrival shot. You commit the route before moving.

name: Rear Guard
description: Action 1 commits backward from your aim. Fire its original follow-up round halfway through and intercept at most one visible hostile projectile in the short forward lane. Other shots and fixed hazards remain dangerous.

name: Cartridge Drill
description: Earn action 2: load up to four missing rounds individually while walking. Primary fire waits; use action 2 again to stop with completed rounds retained. Fresh burst/step, dodge, ordinary reload or health damage interrupts.

name: Roving Chamber
description: Keep the same finite Cartridge Drill running through fresh Precision Burst and Passing Shot, including either early fork. Coordinate three actions without gaining extra rounds, faster loading or immunity.

name: Ready Round
description: The first actual Cartridge Drill insertion opens a short paid Passing Shot. Spend one magazine round for the existing step shot without a burst opening, while respecting its recovery. A normal ready burst follow-up stays free.

name: Running Volley
description: Spend a loaded step opening during Passing Shot recovery. Once per drill, completing the first paid step and actually inserting three rounds earns a brief second paid step. Each spends one round and keeps the owned movement/fire/guard variant.

name: Bank Shot
description: Spend one magazine round on a deliberate shot that reflects from one masonry face. Plan the angle through real cover; a second wall stops it. Uses action 1 instead of the Skirmisher discipline.

name: Double Bank
description: Carry Bank Shot through a second real masonry contact. Its original lifetime and travel budget stay finite; a third wall absorbs it. Choose this instead of Line Drive.

name: Line Drive
description: After its first real bank, the shot can pass through one ordinary hostile body. Bosses, weak points and further cover still stop it. Bodies before the bank still intercept. Choose this instead of Double Bank.

name: Measured Pair
description: Action 2 spends one actual round on a bank shot and starts twelve seconds of recovery. Its first real cover contact earns 1.2 seconds to manually aim and spend one further round with action 2. At most two shots; the second cannot earn another. Both inherit your chosen bank variant.

name: Held Measure
description: After Measured Pair earns its second shot, begin one real manual Reload to keep that opportunity through the reload and 0.6 seconds afterward, at most four seconds total. It cannot be reserved twice. Dodge, channel, overdrive, weapon or technique loss cancels the reserved opportunity. The normal reload still takes its full time; no extra rounds are created.

name: Angle Relay
description: Only the second paid Measured Pair shot's first real cover bank earns 0.8 seconds for one paid Bank Shot during its recovery. Spend one real round and extend, rather than reset, the existing Bank Shot recovery. An ordinary ready shot consumes the same opportunity. No automatic shot or recursive proof.

name: Twin Lanes
description: When using an earned Angle Relay during Bank Shot recovery, spend two actual rounds to fire two physical bank shots ten degrees to either side of your manual aim. Both inherit your chosen bank variant and use real cover, bodies, travel and armor. Both projectile slots must fit or nothing is spent. One release consumes the relay and extends recovery; neither shot earns another opportunity. Ordinary ready Bank Shot remains one round.

name: Cooked Canister
description: Press action 1 to prepare one canister and start ten-second base recovery. Press again to throw along your manual aim. Its 2.4-second fuse keeps running while held or moving; holding to expiry safely vents the canister and spends the recovery. A normal cast starts at 650 pixels/second, slows on the floor, and stops at bodies or cover before its 90-pixel, 80-base-damage blast. Cover and source-sensitive armor apply. A live hand blocks primary fire until you throw or cancel; firing, Reload, dodge, actual health loss, burst or overdrive interrupts it. No friendly damage, ammunition refill or extra resource. Choose this discipline instead of Skirmisher or Marksman.

name: Skimming Case
description: The thrown canister banks once from real fixed cover, retaining the unused portion of that tick and eighty percent of its speed. A further wall or a body grounds it; the same finite fuse continues. Excludes Contact Case.

name: Contact Case
description: A thrown canister bursts on its first physical body or cover contact instead of waiting on the floor. It cannot bank, seek a target or pass cover. Manual cooking still sets how long it can travel before the fuse expires. Excludes Skimming Case.

name: Underhand Cast
description: Action 2 makes a short cast at 280 pixels/second. It can release the canister already in your hand, or prepare and cast a fresh one in a single press if the same recovery is ready. Floor drag, bodies, cover and the actual remaining fuse still apply; no second stock or recovery is created.

name: Re-pin Drill
description: One Reload press may re-pin a live hand canister for at most four seconds, freeing the hand. The remaining fuse is stored exactly, never rewound. Action 1 resumes that same canister; it may not be re-pinned twice, including after a later catch. Ordinary magazine reload is separate. Excludes Clipped Sling; this preparation choice is optional before Toe Roll.

name: Clipped Sling
description: Keep the live hand canister while using your issued Precision Burst and its owned General transformations. Its fuse keeps running; this grants no burst damage, free ammo or recovery. Primary fire, ordinary Reload, dodge, health loss and overdrive still interrupt it. Excludes Re-pin Drill; this offensive timing choice is optional before Toe Roll.

name: Toe Roll
description: Action 2 near your own grounded canister kicks that actual object along manual aim at 420 pixels/second. You must be within 48 pixels with a clear path. One kick per canister; its remaining fuse, casing choice and spent recovery stay exact. A nearby eligible grounded canister takes priority over a fresh short cast. No teleport, new charge, targeting or fuse refresh.

name: Live Return
description: Action 1 can catch your own grounded canister within 48 clear pixels when at least 0.2 seconds of fuse remains. It returns the same object to your hand for another manually aimed throw. One catch per canister; its remaining fuse, spent kick/re-pin rights, casing and recovery are retained. Pool rejection cannot eat the held charge. No new explosive, stock or rewound clock.

name: Settled Shot
description: Action 1 reserves one actual magazine round and starts ten-second base recovery. Stand still for 0.7 seconds, then press action 1 again to fire a manually aimed, direct 110-base-damage physical shot. Preparation lasts at most three seconds and never fires automatically. Turning more than twelve degrees from the settled bearing recenters the sight and restarts settling within the original deadline. Movement, a new primary press, Reload, dodge, health loss, burst or overdrive cancels the paid preparation without refund. A held primary stays blocked through preparation; release and press it again to cancel. Let an already committed burst finish before preparing. Cover, bodies, travel and source armor apply; no bank, piercing, targeting or immunity. Choose this discipline instead of Skirmisher, Marksman or Grenadier.

name: Careful Carry
description: Movement can carry the same paid Settled Shot round within its original three-second preparation. Every actual displacement moves the sight to your current position, recenters its bearing and restarts the full0.7-second settle. Stop and settle before separately releasing; there is no moving release, extra speed, protection or deadline extension. Fresh preparation still requires a planted body. Reload, dodge, actual health loss, channel, burst, overdrive or a new primary press after release still abandons the round. Choose this handling instead of Clear Chamber.

name: Clear Chamber
description: During valid Settled Shot preparation, press Reload to return exactly its one reserved round into available magazine space. This cancels preparation and keeps the spent recovery; that press clears the chamber rather than starting an ordinary reload. A full magazine rejects the clear and preserves the paid preparation and original deadline. A later Reload without preparation works normally. Firing, expiry, movement or another interruption returns nothing. Choose this handling instead of Careful Carry.

name: Bore Through
description: After preparing and settling Settled Shot, action 2 releases the same paid round with70base ability impact instead of110. It may cross one narrow cover section, at most68pixels along its actual path including the round's width, then retains sixty percent impact. Travel inside cover consumes real time and lifespan; deeper masonry, another solid or the first body stops it. Armor uses your actual firing origin. This is no body piercing, bank, targeting or armor bypass. It cannot prepare a fresh round, extend the original opportunity, return ammunition or reset recovery. Action 1 keeps its direct shot. Careful Carry and Clear Chamber remain optional handling choices.

name: Field Rest
description: With no paid round prepared, action2 sets an empty rest at your actual position and bearing. Remain planted for0.7seconds; moving, taking health loss or another action interrupts unfinished setup. Once settled you may leave, but the rest stays fixed and expires9seconds after planting. Return within6pixels and12degrees: an accepted fresh action1 consumes the rest and reserves one actual round ready for a separate manual release. Normal recovery and actual ammunition still apply; unavailable preparation preserves the rest. Elsewhere action1 retains its ordinary full settling. Action2 recalls an existing empty rest, or uses Bore Through when a paid round is prepared. Carry movement restarts settling; Clear returns only the paid round, never the rest. No automatic shot, targeting, remote origin, cover, protection, extra ammunition or new currency.

name: Prepared Withdrawal
description: Prepare two separate Field Rest positions at least96pixels apart, each with its real settling, manual bearing and original expiry. Both must be settled before a normally available action1 claims the first. Only a successful separate manual release earns one return opportunity at the other original site. Physically return within its local position/bearing limits: action1 may reserve another actual round during recovery, ready for its own separate manual release. That alternate payment extends spent recovery by one ordinary action1 duration. A normally ready claim consumes the same finite opportunity. With no paid preparation, action2 sets a second site only after the first settles and from sufficient distance; nearer action2, two sites or an armed return means recall the plan. Carry still requires new settling after movement; Clear returns only its reserved round and keeps recovery. No site, right or ammunition is restored and a return cannot earn another return. Physical bodies, cover, time and firing-origin armor remain.

name: Flak Round
description: Spend one magazine round to launch a defensive flak shell along your manual aim. Its 0.6-second fuse or first body/cover contact makes one burst at its actual position. After nearby shots move, the 45-pixel burst clears at most three small hostile projectiles with clear line of sight. It deals no body damage and cannot clear large objects, beams, fields or ground attacks. Protection begins only at the burst; earlier hits remain. Moving and Braced Firing are allowed. Reloading, dodging, channeling, overdrive, empty ammunition or a full projectile pool rejects launch without payment. Ordinary primary pauses for the launch. Base recovery is eight seconds.

name: Close Pattern
description: Fit a shorter 0.4-second fuse and a 60-pixel all-around burst. It reaches less distant ground before bursting, but covers every bearing. One magazine round, at most three small hostile shots and the same recovery; real bodies and cover still stop the shell. Choose this fitting instead of Forward Baffle.

name: Forward Baffle
description: Fit a longer 0.8-second fuse and a 90-pixel forward burst within a 70-degree fan. The fan keeps the original firing bearing and leaves a real rear gap. One magazine round, at most three small hostile shots and the same recovery; real bodies and cover still stop the shell. Choose this fitting instead of Close Pattern.

name: Manual Fuze
description: Use action 2 to burst your one actual flying flak shell at its present position. Command it before the original fuse ends; the burst still waits until nearby shots have moved. It cannot act on the launch moment, create another shell or burst, return ammunition or reset recovery. Busy hands reject the command while the original flight and fuse continue. Without a live own shell there is no action to command. Both optional burst fittings retain their actual geometry.

name: Running Fuze
description: Change your first Action 2 command into one early interception pulse while the same paid shell keeps flying. That pulse may clear at most one actual small hostile shot. The original fuse or first body/cover contact later makes the final pulse, using only the unspent part of the original combined three-shot allowance. An empty early pulse uses no interception allowance, but the command is still spent. You cannot command that shell again. No new round, extra carrier, extended fuse or recovery reset. Choose this handling instead of Hanging Fuze; omitting both keeps the original immediate three-shot Manual Fuze.

name: Hanging Fuze
description: Your first Action 2 command arrests the actual shell at its current air position and firing bearing. It does not burst on that command or extend its original fuse. A separate later Action 2 can burst the same shell there; its original fuse or an actual enemy body contact can still end it. The one burst retains the original three-small-shot allowance and real cover. Busy rejection keeps the arrested shell and original deadline. No teleport, attachment, extra round, persistent mine, refund or recovery reset. Choose this handling instead of Running Fuze; omitting both keeps the original immediate Manual Fuze.

name: Seam Fuze
description: While your paid flak shell is still live, press Action 1 again to cut its flight and clear a thin seam along the ground it actually crossed. The seam reaches 9 pixels to either side and uses only the unspent part of that shell’s original three-small-shot allowance. Action 2 keeps your acquired point-burst operation, so choose a narrow line behind the shell or a wider burst at it. Running Fuze spends from the same allowance; Hanging Fuze retains only the line laid before arrest. Real cover crossing that line permanently severs it for this shell, leaving Action 2 and the original fuse available. Cut before the original fuse ends. Busy hands reject without cutting. No extra round, body damage, shield, recovery reset or lingering trap.

name: Traverse Stroke
description: Start a finite four-round firing stroke with Action 1. The first physical round leaves immediately; three later rounds each require and spend their own actual magazine round over the next second. Walking pauses while the barrel slews toward manual aim, within sixty degrees of its first bearing. Every admitted round recoils your body eight pixels over the following four combat steps, with real cover blocking movement. Another separate Action 1 releases the feed and lets you walk; fired rounds and their recoil remain. Reload, dodge, channeling or overdrive stops unpaid future rounds. Empty or full-pool rejection spends nothing; a failed later slot ends the feed. Primary waits through the stroke. Each round deals 45 base weapon-scaled damage through ordinary bodies, cover, time and armor. Eight-second base recovery starts with the first admitted round. Choose Siege Gunner instead of Flak Gunner.

name: Set Spade
description: Plant this carriage on stable ground before starting a Traverse Stroke: walking input rejects the start without payment. The stroke adds no recoil and keeps its manual barrel slew, while holding walking input. Any actual external ground displacement breaks the post and ends unpaid future rounds; fired rounds remain. Terrain, moving cover and forced movement still apply. The same four actual rounds, original stroke slots and recovery remain. Choose this fitting instead of Floating Cradle.

name: Floating Cradle
description: Walk normally during a Traverse Stroke and retain each paid round’s actual recoil. Every round keeps the initial world bearing: later mouse aim cannot steer the barrel. Relocate the actual muzzle to find new clear lanes, or release the feed when that bearing becomes useless. This grants no movement bonus, protection or extra round and changes no original stroke slots or recovery. Choose this fitting instead of Set Spade.
